question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Cofactor Method To Solve for an Unknown Quantity
question.problem:
The entry ${a}_{33}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & k \\ -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}]$
equals $\frac{1}{4}$ and $det(A)=6+3k.$ Find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=6+3k
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{33}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{33}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{33} & =(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2-(-1) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{33}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{33} \\  & =\frac{1}{6+3k}\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{1}{2+k}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{33}^{′}=\frac{1}{4}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} & =\frac{1}{2+k} \\ 2+k & =4 \\ k & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
